answer: Each new agent identity must post a non-transferable cipher-locked stake that grows linearly with the number of prior identities sharing the same atlas of behavioral fingerprints. During a gale of simultaneous registrations the protocol automatically multiplies the next stake by the current cohort size, so the marginal capital required for the nth fake rises at least linearly. Failed audits slash the entire cumulative stake of the fingerprint cluster, making large-scale sybil farms capital-prohibitive while honest single agents pay only the base amount.
